scores.notes: Both show a lake ringed by steep, olive-terraced hills with stone houses at the shoreline (right bank on the left, far shore on the right) and a mast with a torn sail. The calmer water on the left is the storm-then-calm change the descriptions ask for, and the boat sitting nearer the shore is a viewpoint and drift difference, not a different lake.

On the left, Moses is identifiable by role as the staff-bearing elder who stands beside Aaron, apart from the crowd. He and Moses at the rock (right) share long white hair, a long full white beard and an elderly face. The right face is small and reads slightly lighter, but no identity cue clearly conflicts.

The staff-bearing elder beside Aaron (left), the only figure set apart from the crowd with him, and Moses striking the rock (right) share swept-back long white hair, a long full white beard, a lean lined face and light olive skin.
The staff-bearing elder beside Aaron (left) and the seated Moses (right) share long white hair, a long full white beard, a lined elderly face and the same warm brown skin.

Moses at the rock (left) is clear, but Moses at the sea (right) is seen from behind in lost profile, with only white hair and the edge of a beard showing. Face shape and skin tone, the cues that separate other Moses renderings, cannot be compared.

Both have short grey hair and a grey beard, but Daniel before Belshazzar (left) has light olive skin. Daniel on the rooftop (right) has a deep brown face and hands while his cream tunic stays light, so the skin tone conflicts and is not just shadow.

Peter is clear on the left (grey curly hair, grey beard), but the right description names only 'disciples' and the five men on the shore stand as a group. Picking the bearded man with the staff as Peter would rest on his resemblance to the left image, not on anything that singles him out.
The staff-bearing elder beside Aaron (left), Moses by role, and the seated Moses (right) share wavy shoulder-length white hair, a full white beard, a lined elderly face and light olive skin.

Moses crossing the sea (left) has deep reddish-brown skin and a gaunt, long face. The staff-bearing elder beside Aaron (right), Moses by role, has light olive skin and a fuller face, although both have white hair and beards, so the skin tone conflicts.

Peter leaping from the boat (right) is clear, but the left description names only 'disciples' and the five men on the shore stand as a group. Nothing but resemblance to the right image picks one of them out as Peter.

Both have white hair and a full white beard, but Moses crossing the sea (left) has deep reddish-brown skin and a gaunt face. Moses at the shore (right) has light olive skin even under a darker sky, so the difference is not lighting.
